# Compare-ZbxConfiguration

## SYNOPSIS

Shows what importing a configuration document would change.

## SYNTAX

### Path (Default)

```
Compare-ZbxConfiguration [-Path] <string[]> [-Format <ZabbixConfigurationFormat>] -Rules <ZabbixConfigurationImportRuleRequest> [-Unredacted] [-Connection <ZabbixConnection>] [<CommonParameters>]
```

### Text

```
Compare-ZbxConfiguration -Source <string> [-Format <ZabbixConfigurationFormat>] -Rules <ZabbixConfigurationImportRuleRequest> [-Unredacted] [-Connection <ZabbixConnection>] [<CommonParameters>]
```

### LiteralPath

```
Compare-ZbxConfiguration -LiteralPath <string[]> [-Format <ZabbixConfigurationFormat>] -Rules <ZabbixConfigurationImportRuleRequest> [-Unredacted] [-Connection <ZabbixConnection>] [<CommonParameters>]
```

## DESCRIPTION

The Compare-ZbxConfiguration cmdlet sends a configuration document to the server with configuration.importcompare and writes the differences an import with the same rules would make, object by object, without changing anything. Run it before Import-ZbxConfiguration to review an import. The before side of an updated object carries the server's current values, including plaintext secrets, so a difference with secrets is redacted unless -Unredacted is given.

## EXAMPLES

### Example 1: Preview what an edited template document would change

```powershell
$doc = Export-ZbxConfiguration -Template 'Web App' -Format Yaml
$edited = $doc -replace 'description: .*', "description: 'Shop front end, v2'"
$diff = $edited | Compare-ZbxConfiguration -Format Yaml -Rules @{ Templates = @{ UpdateExisting = $true } }
$diff.templates.updated | ForEach-Object { '{0}: {1} -> {2}' -f $_.after.template, $_.before.description, $_.after.description }
```

configuration.importcompare: the result lists, per object family, what would be added, updated (before/after) or removed with these -Rules. Nothing is changed on the server. The server compares templates (and what they contain) only; a document's hosts are not compared.

### Example 2: Check that a template still matches its saved file

```powershell
$path = Join-Path ([IO.Path]::GetTempPath()) 'web-app.json'
Export-ZbxConfiguration -Template 'Web App' -Path $path
if (-not (Compare-ZbxConfiguration -Path $path -Rules @{ Templates = @{ UpdateExisting = $true } })) { 'in sync' }
Set-ZbxTemplate -InputObject 'Web App' -Description 'changed by hand' | Out-Null
$drift = Compare-ZbxConfiguration -Path $path -Rules @{ Templates = @{ UpdateExisting = $true } }
$drift.templates.updated | ForEach-Object { 'drifted: {0} is now "{1}", the file says "{2}"' -f $_.before.template, $_.before.description, $_.after.description }
Remove-Item $path
```

An empty result means the server already matches the document for the families the rules cover; -Path reads the document from a file, in the format its extension names unless -Format says otherwise.

### -Format

The document's wire format: json, xml or yaml. When omitted, a file's extension names it (.json, .xml, .yaml/.yml), else the text's first character does ({ JSON, < XML, otherwise YAML); a file whose extension names another format than -Format is refused (ZabbixConfigurationFormatMismatch) and the other files go on.
